hens_rule_text: 3 chickens allowed for the first 2,000 sq ft of lot, plus 1 more chicken for each additional 1,000 sq ft; no roosters; a zoning permit is required
permit_notes: A same-day zoning permit is required, reported at around $70 after the city lowered an earlier $350 fee; one secondary source instead describes a $300 zoning-variance fee, so the current amount is unconfirmed.
setback_notes: Secondary sources describe coops as generally needing to be 15 to 50 ft from neighboring dwellings and 5 to 10 ft from property lines, but the exact code figures were not confirmed from the primary text.
coop_rules: Feed must be kept in a rodent-proof container; chickens must be confined to the owner's property and not allowed to roam.
zoning_notes: Rule is citywide under Pittsburgh Zoning Code Sec. 912.07.B (Urban Agriculture), adopted as part of a 2016 to 2017 urban agriculture zoning update; a separate ordinance Sec. 635.02 bars letting chickens roam off the owner's property.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: Fireman Creative, City of Pittsburgh Passes New Urban Agriculture Zoning Code
Pittsburgh Post-Gazette (via PressReader), Backyard chickens given approval

research_notes: Only secondary sources (a local advocacy blog, a zoning-news blog and archived news coverage) were found describing Zoning Code Sec. 912.07.B; the two searches gave slightly different chicken counts (3 base vs 5 base per 2,000 sq ft) and different permit fees, and the primary zoning code text could not be opened, so figures should be treated as approximate.
